independent_review_method: Human-agent review of complete fetched source bodies in retrieval-25isk75d, including enclosing API property objects. Not just quote occurrence or model narrative.
review: All ten sampled facts confirmed. Short stored excerpts omit some clauses and the deletion-rule parent path; full source bodies were reviewed. One fixture does not establish universal accuracy.

claims.concept: DATE criteria field types and formats
claims.claim: DATE criteria supports five date format types: ISODATE (ISO-8601 formatted date, default), EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS (all Unix epoch timestamps requiring BSON type long), and OBJECT_ID.
claims.basis: The cited Terraform datasource names all five values and ISODATE default. The complete cited standard setup requires BSON long for all three epoch units.

claims.concept: DATE criteria field types and formats
claims.claim: Time series collections only support ISODATE format for the date field value in DATE criteria.
claims.basis: The cited time-series setup requires ISODate for the date value. The fetched API collectionType schema also requires ISODATE for TIMESERIES.

claims.claim: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive DATE criteria supports exactly five date_format values: ISODATE, EPOCH_SECONDS, EPOCH_MILLIS, EPOCH_NANOSECONDS, and OBJECT_ID.
claims.basis: The cited datasource explicitly lists exactly these five values. The standard setup describes ISO date, three epoch units and ObjectId.

claims.claim: The date field used for archival criteria cannot be modified after the online archive is created.
claims.basis: The cited standard setup forbids modifying the date field after archive creation. The time-series setup fixes its time field too.

claims.claim: MongoDB Atlas Online Archive calculates document age using the formula: current_date > dateField + expireAfterDays.
claims.basis: The cited API criteria.dateField description states current date exceeds date-field value plus expireAfterDays days. The cited Terraform criteria section states the same archival condition.

claims.claim: The bounds of 7 to 9215 days apply to dataExpirationRule.expireAfterDays, not to criteria.expireAfterDays.
claims.basis: The complete cited API places the7/9215bounds under dataExpirationRule.expireAfterDays and describes deletion. Its separate criteria.expireAfterDays describes archival eligibility without those bounds. The cited Terraform resource puts the bounds in Data Expiration Rule.

claims.concept: Partition fields constraints for DATE rules
claims.claim: When using DATE criteria, a maximum of three partition fields are allowed: the date field plus up to two additional commonly-queried fields.
claims.basis: The cited Terraform resource permits up to three partition fields when one is date_field. The cited standard setup permits two additional fields. The fetched API requires the date field in DATE partition fields.

claims.concept: Partition fields constraints for DATE rules
claims.claim: Partition field values are limited to a maximum of 700 characters; documents with partition field values exceeding this limit are not archived.
claims.basis: The cited Terraform resource explicitly limits partition values to700characters and excludes longer documents from archiving.

claims.claim: DATE criteria selects a single date field and an age in days; only the age parameter can be modified after archive creation, not the chosen date field.
claims.basis: The cited standard setup defines a date field plus days and fixes the field. The cited yossale article explicitly permits changing only days within Date Match. This claim is about those criteria, not unrelated archive settings.

claims.claim: Custom Criteria accepts standard MongoDB query filter expressions to define archival conditions.
claims.basis: The cited overview describes a custom MongoDB query that selects archived documents. The fetched standard setup invokes db.collection.find(filter). This does not claim every operator or an empty filter is supported.
